What each is for:

- **Keep** — the heart of the town: storehouse, first household, last defence.
- **House** — Homes for townspeople. Fed residents pay tax and newcomers move in; every worker, carrier, builder and recruit comes from a house.
- **Storehouse** — A second store of the town's goods. Carriers take finished goods to whichever store is nearest and fetch from it, so a village far from the keep stops costing long walks. A long timber barn on a stone footing, crates, barrels and sacks under a lean-to.
- **Market** — Trades with passing merchants: a lot of ten of any good sold for 60% of its worth in gold, or bought for 160%. A way out of a stalled chain, not a way to get rich. Stalls under striped awnings round a market cross, crates and barrels.
- **Tavern** — The innkeeper draws the ale the brewery makes and sells it: gold besides the tax. A long low inn with benches and a sign out front, barrels by the door.
- **Chapel** — While one stands, every regiment of the side fights with more heart (+6 morale). A small stone chapel with a bell-cote and a churchyard wall.
- **Well** — Houses within 40 m take in newcomers a quarter sooner; it will put out fires once buildings can burn. A stone well-head under a small roof, a bucket on its rope.
- **Woodcutter's Lodge** — The woodcutter walks into the trees and comes back with timber: the material of every building, of bows and of siege engines. An open shed of stacked logs, fresh trunks by the track, a chopping block and a sawhorse in the yard.
- **Sawmill** — Saws logs into planks (2 timber → 2 planks). From the second level on, every building takes half its timber as planks, so a growing town needs one. A water-wheel saw under an open roof, logs waiting on skids and planks stacked to dry.
- **Forester's Hut** — The forester walks the young wood round his hut: he sets a sapling by any bare stump and works round the saplings so each grows sooner — the wood the woodcutters fell comes back faster. A small lodge with a nursery bed of saplings in rows.
- **Hunter's Lodge** — The hunter stalks in the woods and brings back a carcass: meat and a hide, before the town can afford pigs. Hides stretched on frames, a carcass on the rack, antlers over the door.
- **Quarry** — Cuts building stone from an outcrop: stone for workshops, the barracks and roads.
- **Farm** — The farmer breaks, sows and reaps strips of land behind the farm. The farmland grows with the farm level, so farms want open ground: build them as a village.
- **Fisher's Hut** — The fisher works the shore of the lake: food that needs no mill or oven.
- **Windmill** — A post mill: grinds grain into flour. The tallest thing in a village; its sails turn while it works.
- **Bakery** — Bakes flour into bread, the staple ration of town and army. A domed oven by the house and a pretzel over the door.
- **Brewery** — Brews ale from grain (2 grain → 2 ale) for the tavern. A brewhouse with a copper under a smoke hood, casks stacked in the yard.
- **Pig Farm** — Fattens pigs on grain: meat for the butcher, hides for the tanner.
- **Butcher** — Turns meat into sausages; a sausage feeds two.
- **Vineyard** — A vintner's press-house with rows of vines behind it. The vines are planted once and bear every season without new sowing; they take up land like a farm's fields.
- **Winery** — Presses grapes into wine in a stone cellar of barrels. Wine is carried to the houses: a household with wine pays more tax and grows faster.
- **Tannery** — Turns hides into leather armour for the lower tiers of the army.
- **Iron Mine** — Digs iron ore from an ore outcrop. A timbered adit in a knoll of rock, rails, an ore tub and the ore heap.
- **Smelter** — A bloomery: smelts iron ore into iron, burning timber as charcoal. A squat stone furnace, bellows, smoking charcoal and heaps of slag.
- **Smithy** — Forges weapons from iron, burning timber. Open to the street: the glowing hearth and the anvil are seen from afar.
- **Armourer** — Makes mail from iron for swordsmen, halberdiers and knights. Armour stands, a rack of polearms and shields in the town's colour outside.
- **Fletcher** — Makes bows and crossbows from timber.
- **Stable** — Raises war horses on grain.
- **Barracks** — Townspeople called up walk here, take their equipment and form a regiment. Its level decides which units can be trained.
- **Gun Foundry** — Casts the guns: field cannon at level 1, mortars at level 2, from iron, timber and stone. Like the barracks it has no worker; a gun's crew comes from the town. A stone casting house with a tall furnace stack, a casting shed and a new gun on show in the yard.
- **Watchtower** — A stone tower for up to 4 archers or crossbowmen of one kind, who shoot from its top further than from the ground. It may stand anywhere: by the town, an outlying mine or a village.
- **Road** — drawn from point to point; carriers, workers and builders take it whenever it shortens the walk.
- **Wall** — drawn from point to point like a road; it blocks people and soldiers of both sides, so leave a gap where your own must pass.

Rules common to all buildings:

- **The keep's levels.** Level 1: reach 280 m (farms 340 m), barracks up to level 1, 1800 hit points, an arrow every 1 s. Level 2: reach 330 m (farms 390 m), barracks up to level 2, 2600 hit points, an arrow every 0.75 s; costs 250 gold, 60 wood, 120 stone. Level 3: reach 380 m (farms 440 m), barracks up to level 3, 3600 hit points, an arrow every 0.5 s; costs 500 gold, 100 wood, 240 stone. Raising it takes 60 s.
- **Free placement.** A building goes anywhere within 280 m of its side's keep (farms and vineyards
  340 m; woodcutters, quarries, mines and watchtowers anywhere on the map), and no nearer
  than 90 m to the enemy's) where the ground under it rises no more than 2.2 m, is not
  water, and is 1.5 m clear of other buildings and of farm strips. A side may have 64 buildings.
- **Three levels.** Level 3 is the top. A level costs ×1 / ×1.5 / ×2.5 of the base price and works
  ×1 / ×1.6 / ×2.3 as fast; an upgrade takes 15 builder-seconds once its timber and stone are on site.
- **Built by hand.** Gold is paid at once; timber and stone are carried from the keep to the site, and
  up to 3 builders raise the building only as far as the materials delivered allow.
- **One worker each.** A workshop works only while its worker is there; a hungry worker works at half speed.
- **Own stores.** Carriers fill a workshop's inputs up to 8; outputs pile in its yard up to 24, then
  work stops until carriers clear them (they come once 4 lie there).
- **Demolition** returns 50 % of the base price and whatever lay in the yard.

## 3. Production chains

```
Farm ──grain──► Windmill ──flour──► Bakery ──bread──► houses, keep, army
     ├─grain──► Pig Farm ──meat──► Butcher ──sausages──► houses, keep, army
     │                   └─hides─► Tannery ──leather armour──► pikemen, archers, crossbowmen, light cavalry
     └─grain──► Stable ──horses──► light and heavy cavalry
Fisher's Hut ──fish──► houses, keep, army
Woodcutter's Lodge ──timber──► buildings, Smithy, Fletcher, militia shields, cannon
Quarry ──stone──► buildings, roads, mortars
Iron Mine ──ore──► Smelter (+ timber) ──iron──► Smithy (+ timber) ──weapons──► every armed regiment
                                         ├─► Gun Foundry (+ timber, stone) ──► cannon, mortars
                                         └─► Armourer ──mail──► swordsmen, halberdiers, heavy cavalry
Fletcher ──bows──► archers, crossbowmen
```
